## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of Kleene 3-valued semantics, especially how implications propagate under unknowns and how to reach a fixpoint via forward chaining.

## Key Concepts
- Kleene three-valued logic basics
- Implication as (¬a) ∨ b
- Propagation to fixpoint in a finite domain

## Code Example
```javascript
function not(x){return x==='T'?'F':x==='F'?'T':'U';}
function or(a,b){return a==='T'||b==='T'?'T':(a==='U'||b==='U'?'U':'F');}
function imp(a,b){return or(not(a), b);} // Kleene-style
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would results change if a second round could escalate U to T?
- How to implement a generic 3-valued propagator for arbitrary constraint sets?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to reason with three-valued Kleene semantics across time, ensuring no constraint evaluates to F while maintaining at least one unknown (U) value.

## Key Concepts
- **Kleene semantics**: ¬: T↔F, U→U; ∧/∨ as min/max; implication as A→B = max(¬A, B)
- **Time-indexed propagation**: Constraints of the form A_t → B_{t+1} propagate values forward in time
- **Constraint satisfaction**: Working with partial information and explicit time horizons

## Propagation Discussion
The sequence demonstrates how unknown values propagate through constraints without forcing them to F. When P3 or P4 is U, the antecedent of certain rules evaluates to U rather than T, allowing consequent values to remain as U or be determined by other constraints. This partial evaluation chain allows the system to maintain uncertainty while still satisfying all rules—a key property of real-time policy engines handling incomplete information.

Tests practical understanding of Kleene-style 3-valued logic, including how ∨, ∧, ¬, and → behave with U, plus a concrete propagation/backtracking workflow on small constraint graphs.

- Kleene three-valued logic semantics

- Kleene 3-valued logic

```javascript
function not(x){if(x==='T')return 'F'; if(x==='F')return 'T';return 'U';}
function and(a,b){if(a==='F'||b==='F')return 'F'; if(a==='U'||b==='U')return 'U'; return 'T';}
function or(a,b){if(a==='T'||b==='T')return 'T'; if(a==='U'||b==='U')return 'U'; return 'F';}
function imp(p,q){return or(not(p), q);}
```
